faqs.a: Break-even units = Fixed costs ÷ (Selling price − Variable cost per unit). Break-even revenue = Units × Selling price. Contribution margin per unit = Price − Variable cost.

faqs.q: Why must price be higher than variable cost?
faqs.a: If price ≤ variable cost, contribution margin is zero or negative and you can never cover fixed costs. The calculator requires a positive contribution margin.

faqs.q: Does this break-even calculator use AI?
faqs.a: No. Units and revenue are computed with standard cost accounting formulas. Nothing is estimated by a model.

faqs.q: What counts as fixed vs variable cost?
faqs.a: Fixed costs stay roughly constant (rent, salaries, software). Variable costs scale with each unit (materials, packaging, per-order shipping).

faqs.q: Who should use a break-even calculator?
faqs.a: Product founders, retailers, cafés, and manufacturers deciding how many units they must sell before a product or campaign becomes profitable.
Each extra unit adds roughly the contribution margin to profit. The tool shows profit per extra unit after break-even so you can model upside quickly.

ui.disclaimer: Instant local calculation — no AI calls. Results update as you type. Estimates only; verify with your own data.
